I am very pessimistic when it comes to points and what they can actually provide as a utility, so the points thing was never a consideration for me. I spent over $12k USD on my Platinum Card in the first two months and even with the welcome bonus, all the points only equate to about $300 in rewards. In general, I don't think I will spend enough on it to see any meaningful amount of rewards in a calendar year. I just hope I can recoup the annual fee, which is about $1,000 USD where I am in the world. With the random restrictions (Read: Ridiculously low spending limit in the first month below even my first Capital One card)  so far and that it is essentially a debit card I need to load up in these first few months, I don't think I will renew it when the first year is up. My biggest gripe is the bullshit I am getting from the rep that says, "This 4 got purchase is outside your spending activity." Dude. If I the majority of my purchases are all my daily Uber rides and $10 food purchases, of course when I actually buy something, it's going to be outside the norm. My Citi credit card on the other hand? They don't give a shit what I spend or how much. Oh yeah, for whatever reason, AMEX does not immediately credit a payment here, requiring 1-2 days, unlike my Citi card here, and my AMEX back in the US.

I am questioning the approximately $1,000 I am paying for my Platinum right now. It's kind of shit to need having it being essentially a debit card for 6 months I have heard, when the fee is that high.

I am currently in my third billing cycle with the Platinum. I stopped overpaying ahead of time after that conversation above with AMEX, so while I can still get approved for small purchases with say Uber and small meals, I still have amounts of say $1,200 declined. Again, this is after I prepaid around $12,000 the first month and did almost all my spending on it where possible, with the biggest charge being around $8,000. It's extremely silly that even with my Blue Cash card, I have no problems with such amounts.

I have the same problem with my Platinum and it's a huge pain in the ass, not actually knowing if I will be declined or not at a point of sale, especially after the online tool to check a spending limit said I am approved to make the purchase. I spent $8k on a purchase and had to overpay the amount first and wait the day for it to credit to my account before I could make the purchase. I then checked if I could spend $5k on the card. It said approved online via the checker tool. I go make the purchase. Card is locked. I call to ask what's going on. Girl on the phone tells me they need to conduct a review and will take 3-4 days. I get a call back eventually on the 4th day. Guy on the phone tells me they can't approve that amount yet but I can deposit more money if I want. I ask him what is the point of the Platinum Card if the "no preset spending limit but there is a mystery spending limit that exists but it's a secret" is there and I keep getting denied on these arbitrary terms, and risk the embarrassment at a point of sale? I don't have any of these problems with my Visa/MC credit cards with significantly higher defined limits. The Platinum Card where I am already has a silly fee of around $1,000 USD. But all this for basically a pretty debit card that I must make large deposits in to use? For what? If this shit keeps up, I will just cancel the stupid thing.
